items.title: Trade limits: restored macro values are historical
items.body: The restored templates contain 0.0624 BTC for MaxTradeSizeBisq1 and 0.50 BTC for MaxTradeSizeAltcoin. Bisq 1 v1.10.11 clamps trade limits to 0.25 BTC and calculates method limits from the DAO parameter and payment-method risk factor, with additional account restrictions. The historical macro values are not universal current limits; use the limit shown for the actual account and offer.

items.title: Manual payout: local signing
items.body: The restored 2021 Emergency Multisig payout tool guide describes copying private keys into a text file and removing wallet password protection. Bisq 1 v1.10.11 includes a local Locate key in wallet action and local signature generation; the assembly step combines signatures. Sending a seed or private key to the mediator is not part of that workflow. This source check does not validate any payout, signature or broadcast.

items.title: Wallet seed and application data have different scopes
items.body: Bisq 1 v1.10.11 explicitly says the same seed serves BTC and BSQ, but seed words do not replace the database and keys needed to restore application state. The application backup warning also says the copy is not encrypted. Restoring wallet funds is not evidence that payment accounts, signing identity, messages or trade state have been recovered.

items.title: Seed restoration is an emergency procedure
items.body: Bisq 1 v1.10.11 warns to finish trades, close open offers and empty the existing wallet before restoring an older wallet. Its UI warns that restoring an encrypted wallet removes encryption and requires a new password afterward, and explains the role of the original wallet creation date. These warnings are separate from application-data backup requirements; no wallet restore was performed for this review.

items.title: Conflicting payment-reference advice
items.body: The original Bisq Easy page tells buyers both to leave the payment reason blank/use their own name and to insert the trade ID. Bisq 2 v2.1.15's explicit buyer payment-screen rule says blank if possible, otherwise the buyer's own name; never Bisq or Bitcoin. The pinned upstream guide text itself also retains conflicting trade-ID wording. This check identifies the contradiction and follows the actual payment-screen rule; it does not silently remove either original passage.

items.title: Bisq 1 payment references
items.body: Bisq 1 v1.10.11's rules say to leave the reason blank and not include the trade ID, Bitcoin, BTC or Bisq. Its UI guidance allows an account name or a non-descriptive character when a reference is compulsory and tells traders to discuss alternatives in trade chat. A method-specific old suggestion such as a SWIFT conversion comment is not a universal exception to those rules.

items.title: Bisq Easy amount eligibility differs from the old minimum score
items.body: Bisq 2 v2.1.15 retains a 600 USD Bisq Easy ceiling, but permits seller offers from 1,200 reputation points and computes the amount from 200 points per USD, subject to its rounding and tolerance checks. The old 10,000-point minimum in Reputation2 is not the release-pinned predicate. These rules do not guarantee that a trade or a particular counterparty is safe.
